# Create an employee figure

Create recognizable, interactive Symphony employees. Use `AgentFigureComponent`,
the existing real activity projection and FLAMOX-compatible v2 sprites. The product
calls them employees or figures. Keep Mosaik unchanged.

## Prepare identity and the authoritative tools

Read `resources/figures/README.md`, inspect all four original OpenDots PNGs, and read
[the production brief](references/plush-brief.md) and
[Symphony's state mapping](references/employee-states.md). Preserve existing IDs,
appearance choices, custom PNGs and CLI-independent identity.

Use a Python runtime with Pillow. Locate the installed Codex toolkit:

```sh
python3 .agents/skills/create-employee-figure/scripts/codex_sprite_tool.py locate
```

Read the returned `skill` and `contract` before generating or repairing sprites.
The adapter invokes those actual bundled scripts unchanged. It discovers the
installed `work-pets` plugin or accepts `SYMPHONY_CODEX_SPRITE_SKILL`; it neither
vendors its proprietary implementation nor edits the installation. If unavailable,
stop generation and report the prerequisite. Never invent a replacement compositor,
shape-only validator, successful report or sprite poses drawn by code.

Adapt the destination and integration of `create-pet`: store runs under
`output/imagegen/employee-<identity>-v2`, selected assets under `resources/figures`,
and inspect them in Symphony. Do not create, upload, select or update a ChatGPT Pet,
use a Pets Library folder, or modify another app. Keep the Codex generation,
extraction, identity, direction and motion QA gates.

Maintain a visible four-step checklist: references and tools; canonical identity;
animation and look poses; validation and Symphony integration. Mark completion
only after its evidence exists.

## Generate grounded animation

Run `codex_sprite_tool.py prepare_pet_run` with name, description, plush style,
all identity references and a run directory. Read its request, jobs, prompts and
selected chroma key. An explicitly requested, inspected original OpenDots PNG can
serve as the approved canonical base; record this reuse in the run manifest. New
characters require an imagegen-generated canonical base first.

Keep style references distinct from identity references. For a new employee, the
four original OpenDots PNGs can define the base's visual family without defining
the new character's identity. Record that role explicitly in the run request and
base job. After approving the generated canonical, use it as the sole identity
reference for later jobs; retain the original style references as base provenance.
Keep the unchanged native canonical, exact actual prompt and any deterministic
alpha-cleanup/uniform-fit report. Never silently replace the source with its export.

Use the built-in `$imagegen` workflow for every visual or visual repair. Attach the
approved canonical identity, every identity-defining reference and the matching
layout guide. Generate one state strip per job, never a whole atlas. Preserve
plush fibres, face, silhouette, tiny limbs, accessories, camera and lighting. Do not
flatten the character into Memphis geometry or apply palette filters to create a
different employee. Final assets require actual alpha. Opaque contrasting chroma
is permitted for intermediate strips when native-alpha extraction leaves debris.

When independent jobs are ready, delegate one visual job per worker and keep up to
three visual workers active. Each returns the selected source and honest frame-count,
identity, background, padding, clipping and detached-effect QA. The parent owns
deterministic assembly and acceptance. Generate `idle` and `running-right` early.
Generate the remaining distinct states independently. Derive `running-left` only
by mirroring each approved rightward frame when identity, accessories and lighting
remain correct; otherwise generate it separately.

Immediately run `extract_strip_frames --method auto`, then `inspect_frames
--require-components` for each source row. Fix known failures before proceeding.
Do not slice uneven source spacing into assumed equal slots, scale each pose
independently, erase jump height, reuse one state's poses for another, or pass off
a moving still image as animation. If independently fitted rows change body size
between idle and jumping, use `scripts/register_employee_rows.py` on the extracted
frames. It applies one documented transform per row, keeps the complete jump
displacement and emits registration evidence; it neither draws poses nor composes
an atlas. Re-run the bundled frame inspection on its output. After all nine states
pass, run the bundled compose, contact-sheet and motion-preview commands.

For looks, record character-specific gaze mechanics, generate and approve the four
viewer-relative cardinals (up, right, down, left), then generate and register the
complete row 9. Approve it before generating row 10 using the approved cardinals
and registered row 9. Repair a bad look as a coherent row, never an invented one-off
cell. If a generated second look row has a different body scale, measure the
registered body heights and resize the entire source strip uniformly before the
bundled shared registration. Preserve its original source, hashes, dimensions and
scale factor as evidence. Never fit individual look cells independently.
Follow the exact Codex contract for 8 columns, 11 rows, 192 × 208 cells,
1536 × 2288 final dimensions and all sixteen clockwise 22.5-degree look directions.

## Accept the exact pixels

Run every mandatory bundled gate through `codex_sprite_tool.py`, in this order:

1. `despill_chroma_edges` exactly once on the assembled source, saving the report.
2. `validate_atlas --require-v2 --chroma-key <selected key>` on the final encoded PNG.
3. Final contact sheet, direction QA sheet and direction continuity measurement.
4. Visual review at employee size; record all sixteen expected/observed/verdict
   entries and concrete face landmarks in the semantic report.
5. `validate_pet_quality` with the final atlas and all required reports; require
   actual `ok: true`. If isolated reviewers are available, run the bundled blind
   direction review; cardinal disagreement blocks acceptance.

Render the contract's state GIFs, combined GIF/MP4, idle→jump→idle loop, ordered look
loop, labeled all-row contact sheet, neutral-plus-look sheet and timestamped motion
stills. Use `scripts/render_employee_previews.py --atlas <final PNG> --output-dir
<run>/qa/final-previews` for the state previews through the Codex toolkit plus the
combined motion artifacts (requires ffmpeg). It crops the exact encoded atlas and
never redraws a character. Show motion before calling the result accepted. Fix deterministic extraction
or registration errors deterministically; regenerate only incorrect source imagery.
After the same failure twice, change strategy. Never waive clipping, ambiguous or
wrong directions, reversed motion, identity drift, detached limbs or invalid bytes.

Keep prompts, generated strips, manifests, reports and previews in the run directory.
Record the toolkit version, original-art revision, exact final hash and the validated
asset in `resources/figures/README.md`. OpenDots published no generation recipe at
the inspected revision; these prompts and animations are Symphony-authored.

## Integrate and verify Symphony

Reuse the approved canonical PNG as catalogue thumbnail and startup/error fallback;
keep custom-image support. Ship the selected `<character>-v2.png` beside it. Preserve the MIT
notice for original art and derivatives. Keep animated assets local and available
on desktop and mobile. New identity values must agree in both appearance schemas.
Keep the original default ID-hash palette frozen when adding catalogue entries,
so existing employees retain their appearance. Add new identities as explicit
saved choices and verify Desktop, Mobile, persistence and packaged bytes together.

Drive poses from actual `IAgentActivity` and its running role. Hover, gaze, drag and
greeting affect visual interaction only. Real working/waiting loops remain active
until their event changes; completion and greetings finish; pause, block, failure
and stale data freeze. Reduced motion disables playback and gaze. Stop timers for
offscreen figures, hidden documents and destroyed components. Use existing work
detail and feedback commands for employee actions rather than a fake chat service.

Update frontend Adopt/Adapt/Differ decisions, packaging byte checks and affected
acceptance journeys. Run `yarn agents:sync`, wait for it to finish, then run
`yarn agents:check`, relevant checks, Electron journeys and packaging. Show the
actual motion and report the saved assets, prompts, real validation and limitations.

For a requested static/custom PNG only, retain the lighter read-only
`scripts/validate_figure.py` check. It does not validate a sprite atlas or motion.
